text:
maria: Heads up — seeing a spike of apiserver 503s and controller-manager restarts in us-west2 starting ~10:34 UTC. Affects GPU provisioning jobs; several node pools failed to register.

jamal: +1, I noticed the etcd leader changed 3x in 2 minutes around the same time. kube-scheduler logs show a flurry of connection resets.

maria: Minimal context: large batch of GPU node boot churn from autoscaler and a transient network flap between control-plane subnets.

leo: Copied logs: 
```
I0619 10:34:12.123456 1 apiserver.go:123] http: proxy error: dial tcp 10.0.12.7:2379: i/o timeout
E0619 10:34:13.654321 1 controller_manager.go:98] leader lost: timed out waiting for leader election
```

jamal: sre-bot created incident INC-20240619-1 : https://incidents.example/INC-20240619-1 : assigned to eng-sre oncall.

esther: Quick mitigation suggestions? We have a bunch of pending GPU scaleups for training jobs — should we temporarily route new provisioning to eu-west1 fallback pool? That will increase cross-region egress but keeps jobs running.

maria: I already set autoscaler annotation to prefer eu fallback for the GPU pool (patched 10:42). New scaleups go to eu-west1.

leo: For immediate stabilization I bumped etcd election timeout from 500ms -> 2s for the control-plane instances in us-west2 (deploying now). This should stop flapping while network recovers.

jamal: Confirmed controller-manager stopped restarting after the election timeout bump. Apiserver 503s dropped to baseline. Still seeing a handful of webhook timeouts though.

esther: Can we also add a short-term routing policy in smart-router to prefer dedicated capacity when apiserver health is degraded? That would avoid hitting control-plane for status checks from the provisioner.

maria: Good call. I added a canary routing rule: if apiserver error rate > 5% then provisioner -> dedicated-pool. Applied at 10:55 UTC.

jamal: Cost note: routing to dedicated will spin up reserved GPUs and could double short-term infra cost if sustained. We should estimate burn and align with finance for emergency budget if this persists.

esther: I'll draft a brief note for finance and Eng Leadership. Also want a postmortem — owner volunteer? @maria take lead, @leo do kernel tunings and follow-up on election timeouts, @jamal handle routing/fallback automation.

maria: I'll take the postmortem. Initial timeline + mitigations in the incident ticket. Will schedule a follow-up with product to discuss Reserved vs On-demand fallback policy to control cost.

sre-bot: Incident INC-20240619-1 status -> mitigated (2024-06-19T10:59:47Z).

leo: Action items:
- increase election timeout across control-planes to reduce sensitivity to short network blips
- add automated fallback for GPU provisioning to cross-region pool when controlplane-error-rate > threshold
- run chaos test simulating subnet-level packet loss to validate tolerances

maria: Agree. I'll also add a perf dashboard for apiserver 95th/99th p99 for provisioning-related endpoints so we detect regression earlier. :mag_right:

jamal: Thanks all. I'll post a short status update in #incidents and pin the incident link.

esther: Nice quick triage — saved a bunch of training jobs. We'll reconvene in the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
